    What does DBB mean?
    An AI Overview is not available for this searchCan't generate an AI overview right now. Try again later.
    AI Overview
    DBB most commonly refers to
    Design-Bid-Build, a traditional construction project delivery method where design, bidding, and construction occur in sequential phases. The owner hires a designer to create 100% complete documents, then selects a contractor through competitive bidding, usually leading to fixed-price, low-bid contracts. 
    Key Details About Design-Bid-Build (DBB): 
    • Process Phases:
      1. Design: Owner hires an architect/engineer to create full design documents.
      2. Bid: The completed project goes out for competitive bidding by general contractors.
      3. Build:
        The contract is awarded (usually to the lowest bidder) and construction begins.
    • Key Characteristics:
      • Linear Process: Work is done in distinct, separate stages.
      • Owner Risk: The owner holds separate contracts with the designer and contractor, bearing the risk for design errors or construction delays.
      • High Control: Owners maintain a high level of control over the design and final product, often used in public projects.
    • Advantages: Widely understood, allows for complete design before construction, and typically results in lower initial bid costs.
    • Disadvantages: longer total project duration, and potential for adversarial relationships between designers and builders. 
    Other Potential Meanings of DBB: 
    • Double Block and Bleed (DBB) Valve: An industrial valve configuration providing high-safety isolation for pipelines using two seals and a vent, according to YouTube and Max-Air Technology.
    • IBM Dependency Based Build (DBB): A framework for automating the build of traditional z/OS applications (like COBOL/PL/I) within DevOps pipelines, per IBM.

      What does DBB stand for in business?
      Design−bid − build (DBB) is the traditional method of project delivery and has been the most widely used since ancient times. It is also the one with which project owners are most familiar. DBB is a linear process where one task follows completion of another with no overlap.
